question.text: Per NISM Ch 1.4.1, which statement about the real risk-free rate is CORRECT?

answer.text: The real risk-free rate equals the 10-year G-sec yield plus the repo rate.
The real risk-free rate is always higher than the nominal risk-free rate in inflationary environments.
The real risk-free rate is a SEBI-published monthly number used for AIF hurdle-rate calibration.
The real risk-free rate is the basic rate of return assuming no inflation and no uncertainty about future cashflows; it is the compensation paid for postponing consumption.

explanation.text: The Logic: The real risk-free rate is the basic return assuming no inflation and no uncertainty about future cashflows; it is the compensation paid for postponing consumption. The Trap: Option A invents a formula. Option B reverses the nominal-versus-real relationship - in inflationary environments, nominal exceeds real. Option C fabricates a SEBI publication of the real risk-free rate. Note: Source pages 20-21 of FINAL Series XIX-C AIF Managers (Dec 2025) workbook.
